chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id, Ibn 'Uqdah the historian, narrated: He said, Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn Al-Ju'fi narrated to me: He said, 'Abdullah ibn Jabalah narrated to us: He said, 'Amr ibn Ilyas narrated to us: He said:

My father performed Hajj with me while I was a suckling infant, and my mother died while she was also a suckling infant. I said to my father, 'I will make my Hajj on behalf of my mother.' He said, 'How can that be, when you are a suckling and your mother is a suckling?' So my father entered upon Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) with me, and said, 'May God improve you. I have taken this son of mine for Hajj, and he is a suckling, and his mother died while she was a suckling. He claims that he will make his Hajj on behalf of his mother.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Good. It is for her mother as an extra reward, and it is a valid Hajj for him.'

key_terms.حَجَّةٌ: A valid Hajj (performance of the ritual).
key_terms.صَرُورَةٌ: Suckling infant; one who has not yet reached the age of discernment (tamyiz).
key_terms.فَضْلٌ: Extra reward; additional merit beyond the obligation.

ai.seo_question: Does a child perform Hajj on behalf of a mother who died before reaching the age of discernment?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the juristic principle that a child who performs Hajj for a deceased parent who died before reaching the age of discernment (bulugh) fulfills the obligatory duty for the parent while simultaneously earning the reward for themselves. Imam al-Sadiq’s response clarifies that such Hajj serves a dual purpose: it discharges the debt of the deceased and constitutes a valid, independent act of worship for the child, a ruling derived from the child's capacity to act on behalf of another despite their own minority.
